newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ trade balance deteriorates in Sept - SNZ.
newsitem.headline: NZ trade balance deteriorates in Sept - SNZ.

text.p: The trend estimate for New Zealand's trade balance deteriorated in August and September, following a period of steady improvement between February and July, Statistics New Zealand said on Thursday.

From a low point in February, the exports trend continued to improve until flattening out over the last two months. The trend in imports has been slowly rising each month since the beginning of the year, SNZ said.
The export trend rose two percent in the year to September, against a one percent rise the previous year.

In contrast, the imports trend has shown sustained growth of less than one percent per month since the beginning of the year. In the year to September it rose three percent, against a four percent rise the previous year.

The trade deficit for the September month was NZ$295.9 million, compared with a deficit of NZ$257.3 million a year ago. In the year to September, the deficit was $704.2 million, against $557.1 million in the year to September 1995.
The September quarter trade deficit was $776.3 million, which SNZ said was the largest deficit recorded for a September quarter since 1984.
If large irregular items were excluded, the deficit for the quarter would have been $670.9 million.

SNZ said the unadjusted value of exports in September was $1.53 billion, down 3.2 percent from a year ago. Falls in wood pulp exports (down $27 million) and meat and edible offal (down $23 million) contributed most to the decrease. Dairy exports were up $79 million, and mechanical machinery up $16 million.

Unadjusted imports for September were worth $1.83 billion, down 0.6 percent on a year ago. Major imports included mechanical machinery (valued at $284 million) and vehicles ($226 million). -- Wellington newsroom (64 4) 473 4746
